gates.citation: TESA example TMS-EEG data (Rogasch et al., NeuroImage 2017;147:934; figshare 3188800, GPL 2.0+). Reference impl: MNE-Python (Gramfort et al. 2013, Front Neurosci 7:267) EvokedArray + apply_baseline.

reference.citation: TESA example TMS-EEG data (Rogasch et al., NeuroImage 2017;147:934; figshare 3188800, GPL 2.0+). Reference impl: MNE-Python (Gramfort et al. 2013, Front Neurosci 7:267) EvokedArray + apply_baseline.
reference.description: tepAverage on the real TESA TMS-EEG average recovers the canonical TEP: 6 components in monotonic temporal order, N100 median 115 ms, P180 median 188 ms, mean across-channel polarity match 92.1%; AND an independent MNE-Python reconstruction (mne.EvokedArray + apply_baseline over -200..-20 ms, per-channel peaks in the canonical windows) reproduces the TEP waveform per channel (min correlation 1.000000, max abs diff < 1e-6 uV) and MNE's own N100/P180 median latencies (115/188 ms) + polarity-match (92.1%) match the op (median-latency max abs diff 0). The fold root is the trial-average, so this validates baseline correction + component extraction against MNE; the 150-trial averaging is upstream and captured in the root.
